Name: Academic Search Complete
Description:
Academic Search Complete contains thousands of active global full-text journals that span every conceivable subject area. It also indexes and links to thousands of active global open access journals. Other notable features include a large video library and access to pre-print material from key publishers.

I'd consider Academic Search Complete a general reference database. It's a great place to start researching just about any topic.
Subjects: Basic Information and General Reference|English Language Arts|Mathematics|Science|Social Studies

Name: African-American History
Description:
Covering more than 500 years of the African-American experience, African-American History offers a fresh way to explore the full spectrum of African-American history and culture. Start your investigation of a topic with a video or slideshow overview, use the key content called out on the home page to find an entryway into the database, or dig deep into a subject or era through the Topic Centers. Read about key figures and events, examine famous speeches and other primary sources, and get context from the in-depth timelines. All Infobase products are also cross-searchable, allowing users to locate content across products with a single query.

This is a specialized database with an especially rich set of primary sources and fantastic pathfinders. Think of it as a history-specific enyclopedia. I'd recommend using the browsing tools (especially the topic centers and timelines) to familiarize yourself with a subject before you begin keyword searching.

Name: American Government
Description:
Connecting the origins and structure of U.S. government to historical events and issues, American Government engages students in a meaningful investigation of civics and the American political process. It boasts thousands of primary sources including speeches, letters, newspaper articles, political documents, and landmark Supreme Court cases that illustrate the complexity of questions and debates surrounding the political process, rights and liberties, and domestic and foreign policy.

This is a specialized database that supports guided inquiry: you ask a question that the database materials help you answer. ABC-Clio's academic success corner is integreated into all of their databases and offers fantastic tutorials on core skills like research, writing, reading, and critical thinking that I'd highly recommend.

Name: American History
Description:
American History is a comprehensive resource that spans our nation’s history with a user-friendly interface and award-winning content. The home page offers many ways to begin exploring the material, from the videos, slideshow overviews, and Topic Centers to the lists of key content handpicked by editors to help users find a starting point for their research. By providing the most comprehensive range of information in one complete resource—subject entries, biographies, primary sources, videos and slideshows, images, timelines, and maps and graphs, plus full cross-searchability across all the Infobase history databases—American History offers a virtual library of American history for educators, students, and researchers.

This is a specialized database with an especially rich set of primary sources and fantastic pathfinders. Think of it as a history-specific enyclopedia. I'd recommend using the browsing tools (especially the topic centers and timelines) to familiarize yourself with a subject before you begin keyword searching.

Name: American Indian History
Description:
American Indian History offers fast access to more than 15,000 years of culture and history, covering more than 600 Native American groups through videos and slideshows, images, biographies of key people, event and topic entries, primary sources, maps and graphs, and timelines. With a user-friendly interface, this award-winning database allows for an interactive, multifaceted look at the Indigenous peoples of the Americas. An important feature is full cross-searchability across all the Infobase history databases for an even more comprehensive view of history.

This is a specialized database with an especially rich set of primary sources and fantastic pathfinders. Think of it as a history-specific enyclopedia. I'd recommend using the browsing tools (especially the topic centers and timelines) to familiarize yourself with a subject before you begin keyword searching.

Name: Ancient and Medieval History
Description:
Ancient and Medieval History provides thorough coverage of world history from prehistory through the mid-1500s, with special Topic Centers on key eras, civilizations, and regions, including the ancient Near East, Egypt, Greece, and Rome; ancient and medieval Africa, Asia, and the Americas; medieval Europe and the Islamic World; and much more. Each civilization’s history is brought to life through videos and slideshows, primary sources, maps and graphs, timelines, suggested readings, and suggested search terms. All the Infobase history databases in our collection are fully cross-searchable.

This is a specialized database with an especially rich set of primary sources and fantastic pathfinders. Think of it as a history-specific enyclopedia. I'd recommend using the browsing tools (especially the topic centers and timelines) to familiarize yourself with a subject before you begin keyword searching.

Name: Bloom's Literature
Description:
Bloom’s Literature is a multimedia solution that enriches literature studies with overviews, criticism, author biographies, and background context. In addition to deep analysis, scholarly essays, and multiple interpretations of texts that cultivate critical thinking skills, it also offers audio and video content, essays prompts, and writing guides that assist in crafting strong arguments, structuring ideas, and developing fluent academic writing.

Bloom's is an underutilized resource. Rather than parroting an AI overview or rehashing Sparknotes (or Cliffnotes or LitCharts or whatever), search for a work's title and spend some time reviewing the rich variety of reference works, criticism, character analyses, and other materials available in this specialized database.

Name: Britannica Imagequest
Description:
Britannica ImageQuest provides access to more than 3 million rights-cleared images and 11,000 educational videos drawn from 60+ media partners. All these materials are all cleared for educational, non-commercial use, making them ideal for project-based learning, research, and visual inquiry. This database also includes a built-in citation tool and complete metadata for every image.

If you need a visual and want to be sure it's copyright compliant, make ImageQuest your first destination!

Name: Britannica School
Description:
Comprehensive and authoritative, Britannica School offers over 250 years of articles, images, videos, and primary sources in a single, extremely accessible interface. Most content can scale to three reading levels (Elementary, Middle, and High School).

I'll say something many of you won't like: Britannica is an encyclopedia and, like Wikipedia, should serve as a starting point for high school-level research. Inquiry begins with an encyclopedia. It should never end here.

Oh! And if you're in the habit of Googling your topic and clicking the Britannica link that comes up first, shift platforms to Britanica School! You'll find improved versions of the same articles (and more!) in this database.

Brittanica, like Credo Source and Explora, is the perfect place to start a research project.

Name: Business Source Premier
Description:
New for the 2026-2027 school year!

Business Source Premier offers access to 1,017 active full-text journals with a journal retail value of $598,614.87. It provides researchers with essential business journals such as Harvard Business Review, Academy of Management Journal, Academy of Management Review, Management Science, Marketing Science, MIS Quarterly, Bloomberg Businessweek, Forbes, Fortune, and many others.

Whether you are preparing a DECA pitch, preparing for an FBLA event, analyzing market trends, or studying entrepreneurship, this platform provides the data you need to stand out. You can instantly access deep-dive MarketLine reports for over 15,000 global companies, complete with financial overviews and competitor lists; downloadable SWOT analyses for major brands; preprint articles; case studies; and much more.

Name: Credo Source
Description:
Credo Source is a research starting point and multidisciplinary hub of topic discovery that includes more than 1.7 million reference materials selected specifically for high-school students. Its advanced features, including the Mind Map, Skill Builder video tutorials, and more, are all designed to develop information literacy skills. The wide range of content, Research Skill Builder video tutorials, and integrated federated search empower students to make informed research choices and think critically about where they get their information.

Credo is a phenomonal tool for learning how, exactly, you research a topic. It's a great general reference database for exploratory searching that will help you make connections and build your vocabulary. The Interactive Mind Map is especially cool: it's a graphical representation of related concepts and terms that adds a layer of nuance and understanding to your search.

I'd put Credo in a bucket with Explora and Britannica School as premier destinations for early phases of research.

Name: Culturegrams
Description:
CultureGrams provides country reports that go beyond mere facts and figures to deliver a one-of-a-kind perspective on daily life and culture, including the background, customs, and lifestyles of the world's people. The reports are written and reviewed by in-country experts and are updated as new information becomes available, so you can be sure you are reading nothing but the very best, most current information. CultureGrams contains fore core products:

World Edition: Cultural reports for more than 200 countries. Each include 25 categories such as Land and Climate, History, Personal Appearance, Greetings, Dating and Marriage, Family, Diet, Housing, Holidays, Economy, Education, Health, and more.

Kids Edition: This collection of more than 185+ country reports teaches upper elementary-aged and middle school users about the world around them. Each report includes up-to-date, engaging cultural information, complete with images, an historical timeline, fun facts, and sections on history, population, "life as a kid," and more.

States Edition: These colorful and easy-to-read state reports help upper elementary-aged students understand the diversity and history of each U.S. state and the District of Columbia. Reports include maps, flags, symbols, and timelines, plus sections on history, economy, geography, population, and more.

Provinces Edition: This edition contains kid-friendly reports on all 13 Canadian provinces and territories. Reports include images, maps, charts, data tables, and fun facts, plus sections on the environment, culture, government, first inhabitants, and more.

Although the scope of CultureGrams' content is sharply limited, the quality of its content is second to none, especially given the untimely demise of the CIA's World Factbook.

Name: Curriculum Resource Center
Description:
Curriculum Resource Center gives teachers instant access to thousands of easily reproduced handouts to supplement text and lesson plans used in middle school, high school, and junior college classrooms. This expansive collection contains thousands of fact sheets, timelines, an image gallery, printable maps, full-color science diagrams and experiments, and math activities.

Is somebody actually reading this? Are you a teacher who uses this resource? If so, please tell me! This sort of material is often bundled with our student-facing databases, but the usage data dampens my spirits.

Name: EBSCO eBook Collection
Description:
EBSCO eBooks are online versions of print books our library has either purchased with a perpetual license or via an annual subscription.

While this database offers a pretty solid range of material, it neither captures all of our eBook holdings nor offers the sort of media (journals, periodicals, articles generally) most students are searching for when they visit a database. That said, if you're after a book-length treatment of a topic, give it a go.

Name: ERIC (Education Resources Information Center)
Description:
The Education Resources Information Center, or ERIC, is an online digital library of education research and information. ERIC is sponsored by the Institute of Education Sciences of the United States Department of Education. 

ERIC is freely available through the federal government's eric.ed.gov site, but our EBSCO derivative enhances its index of journal articles, books, conference papers, curriculum guides, dissertations, and policy papers with full-text access, richer search filtering, and the ability to limit by education level and intended audience (teachers, counselors, administrators, etc. 

If you're interested in the art and science of pedagogy (or if you're completing any sort of coursework for professional advancement), you'll find no more comprehensive resource.

Name: European Views of the Americas: 1493 to 1750
Description:
European Views of the Americas: 1493 to 1750 is a free archive of indexed publications related to the Americas and written in Europe before 1750. It includes thousands of valuable primary source records covering the history of European exploration as well as portrayals of Native American peoples.

This archive was co-developed by John Alden and the Curator of European Books at The John Carter Brown Library, Dennis Landis. It represents a wide range of topics, from the British/French/Dutch in America to natural disasters, religious orders, slavery and more. The John Carter Brown Library, founded in 1846, is a foremost repository of rare books and materials and is a center for advanced research in history and the humanities.

If you're interested in doing some primary source analysis to better grasp how Europeans understood the New World, this is a truly invaluable resource.

Name: Explora High Schools
Description:
This interface is designed specifically for high school students according to their needs and search abilities. It's graphically rich and provides access to age-appropriate materials. Includes topic overviews that provide students with a starting point for research and 60,000 top videos from the Associated Press.

I especially appreciate the Topic Explorer pages. Clicking on a category of interest breaks down it into popular, colloquial or curriculum-based subtopics. Clicking on the subtopic brings you to the Topic Page, a unique, dynamic page that includes a Topic Overview article; other available subtopic categories; related Topic Overview articles; a sample of search results on the selected topic; and, when available, a carousel of relevant e-books.

If you're just starting a search, Explora, like Credo Source and Britannica Schools, is a great place to begin.
Subjects: Basic Information and General Reference|Business|Culture and Geography|English Language Arts|Complicated Issues|Health and Wellness|Mathematics|Psychology|Science|Social Studies

Name: FactCite
Description:
FactCite is a collection of award-winning educational databases designed for students from primary grades through high school, supporting research in science, social studies, language arts, and more with age-appropriate, authoritative content. FactCite users may find information using keyword searches or special topic indexes. Favorite features include: text-to-speech, citations, translation, customizable ways to view pages,  and NoodleTools and Google Classroom integration.

If I may speak bluntly, FactCite is primarily a database for elementary and middle-level leaners. If you're hoping to achieve at a high school level, regard it as an early step on the path to more sophisticated materials.

Name: Ferguson's Career Guidance Center
Description:
Ferguson’s Career Guidance Center is a comprehensive resource for career exploration and planning that allows users to quickly find the valuable career information they need, whether it’s industry and professions articles, school planning resources, or skills and career advice. The material draws from a range of authoritative sources, including Encyclopedia of Careers and Vocational Guidance. Curated articles, videos, and tools help users match interests to real-world careers and plan for future success.

Treat Ferguson's as a springboard for career-planning and job-hunting. Complement the federally inflected information available from the Occupational Outlook Handbook with comprehensive, trusted profession and industry profiles that explain job duties, skills, education paths, earnings, employment trends, and more. Rather than relying on AI to generate cover letters and resumes, you can download templates for a variety of cover letter and resume types specialized across industries and job types.

Name: Funk & Wagnall's New World Encyclopedia
Description:
Funk & Wagnalls New World Encyclopedia is a general-purpose reference encyclopedia for students and adults alike. This database indexes over 25,000 records, covering an array of topics across science, history, geography, biography, and the arts.

If you're searching via Explora, Funk & Wagnall's will make up a portion of your search results. These entries tend toward the simplistic, which is a boon if you're after unpretentious summaries, but I'd encourage anyone after a more thorough understanding of a subject to start with the full Explora interface, Brittanica Schools, or Credo to diversify their sources.

Name: Gale eBooks
Description:
Gale eBooks offers a user-friendly experience to explore ebooks on many different issues and topics including history, science, psychology, genetics, and more.

While this database offers a pretty solid range of material, it neither captures all of our eBook holdings nor offers the sort of media (journals, periodicals, articles generally) most students are searching for when they visit a database. That said, if you're after a book-length treatment of a topic, give it a go.

Name: Gale in Context: Biography
Description:
Gale in Context offers more than 650,000 biographical entries covering international figures from all time periods and areas of study. It contains authoritative reference content alongside, videos, audio selections, images, primary sources, and magazine and journal articles from hundreds of major periodicals and newspapers. Continuously updated.

Gale databases offer incredible depth. In this case, their expansive periodical holdings reliably surface multiple perspectives on any given biographical subject, empowering you to compare, contrast, and synthesize information. Rather than taking an encylopedia-style article at its word, use this database to broaden your view of contemporary and historical persons.

Name: Gale in Context: Opposing Viewpoints
Description:
Gale In Context: Opposing Viewpoints is the premier online resource covering today’s hottest social issues, from immigration to fast fashion and artificial intelligence.This cross-curricular research database supports science, social studies, current events, and language arts classes. With over 20,000 pro/con viewpoints, approximately 19,000 reference articles,
interactive maps, infographics, and more, you can prepare to argue any side of an issue.

I'd consider Gale the most capable of the complicated issue databases. Its topic finder helps you make connections between terms and topics that you might not otherwise think of; its highlighting and note-taking tools are helpful if you prefer digital annotation to analog; its depth of content surfaces more competent prose than many written-to-order topic overviews. Use it when style and substance are equally critical considerations.

Name: Gale in Context: US History
Description:
Gale In Context: US History traces America's development from colonization to the present day, It contains millions of articles from periodicals and newspapers; hundreds of thousands of topic and event overviews; biographies; and rich multimedia, including images, videos, audio, and web links. 

Gale's sheer scope and integrated features set it apart from other vendors. Its topic finder helps you make connections between terms and topics that you might not otherwise think of; its highlighting and note-taking tools are helpful if you prefer digital annotation to analog; its depth of content surfaces a wide array of primary and secondary materials on most topics.

Name: Gale in Context: World History
Description:
Gale in Context: World History reaches back to the ancient world — and forward to today's headlines — to deliver a chronicle of the great cultures and societies that have formed the history of the human race. Rare primary sources, reliable reference and multi-media content put this vast topic into context for students. Content is aligned with state and national curriculum standards. Uncover information on hundreds of the most significant people, events, and topics in world history from a variety of sources.

Gale's sheer scope and integrated features set it apart from other vendors. Its topic finder helps you make connections between terms and topics that you might not otherwise think of; its highlighting and note-taking tools are helpful if you prefer digital annotation to analog; its depth of content surfaces a wide array of primary and secondary materials on most topics.

Name: Gale Literary Index
Description:
Gale Literary Index provides quick and easy access to author and title listings from over 130 literature products from Gale and the imprints Charles Scribner's Sons, St. James Press, and Twayne Publishers. The referenced products themselves will contain complete biographies on authors and critical essays on their writings.

Students often find themselves frustrated with Literary Index because they don't fully understand what an index is supposed to do. A literary index is a mere list of works by or about an author. This database does not, alas, necessarily contain the referenced products, which are available from Gale and several affiliated imprints.

In a nutshell, unless you're looking for details about an ouvre, this database won't have much to offer.

Name: Gale Literature: Twayne's Author Series
Description:
Gale Literature: Twayne's Author Series is an ideal starting point for research papers on literary works and figures, special projects and presentations. Students can quickly gain results by searching for a specific author, combining search criteria for a more complex search, or exploring thematic and chronological topics. Find in-depth critical introductions to the lives and works of major writers. Includes influences of literary movements.

If you're working on an author study, interested in webs of influence, or honing in on a school or period, dig in.

Name: Gale Power Search
Description: Gale Power Search is a unified search interface that allows you to search any number of our Gale databases simultaneously.
Subjects: Basic Information and General Reference|Culture and Geography|English Language Arts|Health and Wellness|Mathematics|Psychology|Science|Social Studies

Name: GreenFile
Description:
GrrenFile offers information covering all aspects of human impact on the environment. The scholarly, government, and general-interest titles include content on the environmental effects of individuals, corporations and local/national governments, and what can be done by each to minimize negative impact. Topics covered include global warming, green building, pollution, sustainable agriculture, renewable energy, recycling, and more. GreenFILE is multidisciplinary by nature and draws on the connections between the environment and a variety of disciplines such as agriculture, education, law, health and technology.

Ideal for environmental science, health and wellness, legal studies, and myriad related topics.

Name: Health Reference Center
Description:
Health Reference Center includes comprehensive, in-depth coverage of body systems, current health issues, major diseases and conditions, treatments, and procedures, as well as health and nutrition information specific to men, women, children, teens, and seniors. The up-to-date information comes from hundreds of authoritative sources, plus users can find thousands of videos, illustrations, journal articles from PubMed Central, and reference articles from MedlinePlus.

Beyond its immediate relevance to health and science classes, this is a great resource for making smart decisions about your well-being. Consult these trusted articles and videos on nutrition, mental health, substance abuse, and more in tandem with whatever medical professionals are responsible for your care.

Name: Health Source: Consumer Edition
Description:
Health Source: Consumer Edition covers a wide variety of subjects with nearly 80 full-text consumer health magazines covering nutrition, exercise, medical self-care, drugs and alcohol, and disease. Subjects include fitness, nutrition, diabetes, aging, women's health, children's health, and more.

Look here for both general health information and specific details about ailments, maladies, and condtions.

Name: Health Source: Nursing/Academic Edition
Description:
Health Source: Nursing/Academic Edition is a trusted full-text database covering nursing and allied health topics, including pediatric nursing, critical care, mental health, nursing management, medical law and more. This database is directed at researchers, allied health professionals, nurses, and medical educators. It offers access to full-text scholarly journals focusing on many medical disciplines and also includes a dictionary of medical terminology.

This database is epsecially helpful for health sciences and sports medicine. If you need high-quality medical information, including peer-reviewed studies, you're in the right place.

Name: Issues & Controversies
Description:
Issues & Controversies helps students and researchers understand today’s crucial issues by exploring hundreds of hot topics in politics, government, business, society, education, and popular culture. Presented in a balanced, pro/con format, each article presents the key facts, arguments, history, and current context. An ideal resource for research papers, debate preparation, and persuasive writing assignments.

I'd contend that Infobase's complicated issues database offers the best discovery tools. Make a point of using the subject clusters and browsing options. Their source list is a clever way to identify reliable outlets for all sorts of projects (not only those related to complicated issues!).
Subjects: Complicated Issues|English Language Arts|Current Events and News|Psychology|Science|Social Studies

Name: JSTOR
Description:
JSTOR is a digital library of academic content in many formats and disciplines. The collections include top peer-reviewed scholarly journals as well as respected literary journals, academic monographs, research reports from trusted institutes, and diverse primary sources. JSTOR is part of ITHAKA, a not-for-profit organization that also includes Ithaka S+R and Portico. Its archives run back decades and the curation is second-to-none.

Buy me a hot dog stand since I'm trying to be frank: Jstor is a marvelously seductive database. While it's strongest in the humanities and social sciences, it covers many other subjects as well. It also boasts impressive visual and primary source content. That said, it has two weaknesses: first, recent journal issues are sometimes embargoed, and second, because Jstor is so wonderful, students will search here and nowhere else.

The "one and done" fallacy, long encouraged by out inherent disposition toward laziness and now buttressed by the rising tide of AI-addled interfaces, applies to every database, but be especially wary amidst the siren song that is Jstor.

Name: Learn360
Description:
Learn360 is the ultimate streaming multimedia resource for the K–12 educational market. Users can access more than 137,000 multimedia resources—including high-quality full-length videos, video clips, interactives, images, audio files, articles, activities, worksheets, and more—from more than 200 top educational producers. New content is added regularly.

Great for students, even better for teachers. Give YouTube a rest and take Learn360 for a spin.
Subjects: Basic Information and General Reference|For Teachers

Name: Legal Information Reference Source
Description:
Legal Information Reference Source provides online full text for many of the top consumer legal reference books. It contains more than 310 full-text publications and thousands of legal forms. Many of the full-text legal reference books are provided through Nolo, a provider of legal information for consumers and small businesses.

This database offers the everyday user the necessary tools and detailed “how-to” instructions to independently address a wide-range of legal issues including business law, financial planning, family law, property & real estate and rights & disputes.

If you're trying to bridge the gap between the letter of the law and its actual application, give this database a try.

Name: Library, Information Science & Technology Abstracts
Description:
Library, Information Science & Technology Abstracts (LISTA) is a free research database for library and information science studies. LISTA provides indexing and abstracting for hundreds of key journals, books, research reports. It is EBSCO's intention to provide access to this resource on a continual basis (that is, it's freely available to anyone).

This database is obviously geared toward librarians, but anyone interested in information and informatics, the history of libraries, the perils of resource sharing, and the wooly world of communication would also enjoy it.

Name: Literary Reference Plus
Description:
New for the 2026-2027 school year!

Literary Reference Plus is a full-text literary database providing a complete collection of reference works across all genres and time periods. It contains thousands of poems, short stories, classic novels, plot summaries, critical analysis essays, literary journals, reference books and author biographies, plus lesson plans and literary study guides.

Literary Reference Plus also features dozens of lesson plans and a link to EBSCO's Curriculum Standards Module, a tool that can help teachers in the U.S. and Canada to correlate EBSCO content quickly and easily to Common Core, state- or province-specific curriculum standards. The module provides browsing of specific benchmarks, many which have recommended search strings for successful content retrieval.

Name: Literary Reference Source eBooks
Description:
The Literary Reference eBook Collection is offered as a companion to Literary Reference Source databases, containing reference books from top educational publishers and presses, as well as several classic fiction titles. This encompasses a broad range of literary-related subject coverage, with selections including literary criticism, study guides, and classics such as Emma, Dracula and Frankenstein.

Great if you're looking for a book-length treatment of a literary topic or work; if not, not.

Name: MAS Reference eBook Collection
Description:
Offered as a companion to MAS Ultra - School Edition, this collection contains reference books from top educational publishers and presses. It encompasses a rich selection of titles covering a broad range of general reference subjects, including biography, history, careers, language arts, literature, government, health, math, science, current events and social-emotional health.


Its 500 or so full-text encyclopedias, reference works and e-books offer longer treatments when the depth of coverage a magazine necessitates just won't do.
Subjects: Basic Information and General Reference|Health and Wellness|Science|Social Studies

Name: MAS Ultra - School Edition
Description:
Designed for high school libraries, MAS Ultra – School Edition is a full-text reference database of popular magazines covering many subjects, including history, science and health. It also includes full-text biographies, primary source documents, reference books, and an image collection of more than 2 million photos, maps, flags and color PDFs.

Journalism students and news junkies will benefit from the massive array of periodicals at hand. It's also a primary source repository especially apt for history, political science, civics, government, and politics as well as an avenue for popular science writing and health information.
Subjects: Basic Information and General Reference|Health and Wellness|Science|Social Studies

Name: Masterfile Elite
Description:
Designed specifically for public libraries, MasterFILE Elite provides full-text magazines and reference books covering many subject areas including business, health, education, general science and multicultural issues. It also includes an extensive image collection.

Very similar to MAS Ultra with a good degree of overlap, but MasterFile skews toward a general adult audience rather than high school students.

Name: Masterfile Elite Reference eBook Collection
Description:
The MasterFILE Reference eBook Collection is offered as a companion to MasterFILE databases, containing reference books from top educational publishers and university presses. This encompasses a rich selection of titles covering a broad range of general reference subjects, including biography, history, architecture, literature, cooking, health and wellness, science, self-help, religion, current events, sports, travel and more.

Very similar to MAS Ultra with a good degree of overlap, but MasterFile skews toward a general adult audience rather than high school students.

Name: Medline
Description:
Created by the United States National Library of Medicine, MEDLINE is an authoritative bibliographic database containing citations and abstracts for biomedical and health journals used by health care professionals, nurses, clinicians and researchers. MEDLINE contains journal citations and abstracts for biomedical literature from around the world. The majority of journals selected for MEDLINE are based on the recommendation of the Literature Selection Technical Review Committee.

This is another EBSCO wrapper around a freely available federal resource. Basically, the free version of MEDLINE available through the federal government contains citations, abstractions, and specialized MeSH subject headings. EBSCO's version makes them easier to search and provides links out to full text versions of many (but not all!) indexed articles.

Name: Middle Search Plus
Description:
Middle Search Plus is a full-text database providing popular middle school magazines, reference e-books, and thousands of primary source documents and videos. Subjects include history, current events, science and sports.

Per the name, this database is intended for middle school students.
Subjects: Basic Information and General Reference|Business|Culture and Geography|English Language Arts|Complicated Issues|Health and Wellness|Mathematics|Psychology|Science|Social Studies

Name: Middle Search Reference eBook Collection
Description:
The Middle Search Reference eBook Collection is offered as a companion to Middle Search databases, containing reference books from top educational publishers and presses. This encompasses a broad range of general reference subject coverage for middle school students, with topics including social studies, math, history, language arts, technology, geography, culture and science.

Per the name, this database is intended for middle school students.
Subjects: Basic Information and General Reference|Business|Culture and Geography|English Language Arts|Complicated Issues|Health and Wellness|Mathematics|Psychology|Science|Social Studies

Name: Military and Government Collection
Description:
Military & Government Collection is a database of full-text journals and periodicals pertaining to all branches of the military and government. It is designed to offer current news to military members, analysts, policy makers, students and researchers. Military & Government Collection provides cover-to-cover full text, indexing and abstracts for hundreds of journals and periodicals. Many full-text titles are available in searchable PDF or scanned-in-color.

Not much to say here: if you're after military or government-related information, proceed.

Name: Modern World History
Description:
Modern World History offers a comprehensive look at world history from the mid-15th century to the present. Thousands of subject entries, biographies, images, videos and slideshows, maps and graphs, primary sources, and timelines combine to provide a detailed and comparative view of the people, places, events, and ideas that have defined modern world history.

This is a specialized database with an especially rich set of primary sources and fantastic pathfinders. Think of it as a history-specific enyclopedia. I'd recommend using the browsing tools (especially the topic centers and timelines) to familiarize yourself with a subject before you begin keyword searching.

Name: Newspaper Source Plus
Description:
Newspaper Source Plus provides a full-text digital collection of the world's major news content. It includes millions of articles from newspapers and newswires and offers television and radio transcripts and ongoing daily updates from popular news sources.

Newspaper Source Plus offers full text for more than 460 U.S. newspapers including: The Washington Post, Star Tribune, The Philadelphia Inquirer, Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, Honolulu Star-Advertiser, and St. Louis Post-Dispatch.

Newspaper Source Plus also includes full text for more than 370 international newspapers including: The Sydney Morning Herald, Hindustan Times, Bangkok Post, Toronto Star, The Manila Times, The Jordan Times, and Kuwait Times.

Newspaper Source Plus also includes more than 1.6 million television and radio news transcripts from top sources including: ABC News (American), CBC (Canadian), CBS News, CNBC, CNN, MSNBC, PBS, and Real-Time News.

Newspaper Source Plus brings critical news content with ongoing updates throughout the day. Popular news sources include CNN Wire and Xinhua (China). 

Newspaper Source Plus: get a load of all these newspapers!

Name: Newswires
Description:
EBSCO's Newswires provides near real-time access to top world-wide news from Associated Press, United Press International, PR Newswire, Xinhua, CNN Wire, and Business Wire on a continuous basis. The index to the full text content in EBSCO Newswires is held for a rolling 30-day archive by EBSCO, so users can enjoy the previous 30 days of news relating to their search interests.

Telegraph much? Before the dawn of social media, this is how information spread from a single outlet to many subsidiaries, and the wire persists to the present day. Wires remain common in journalism, public relations, corporate communications, and financial reporting Newswires is useful when you need immediate reporting on an event, topic, or organization. Wire service items are often timely and concise, but lack the depth of investigative journalism or academic scholarship.

Name: NoodleTools
Description:
NoodleTools is an online research management platform that promotes critical thinking and authentic research. Stay organized as you evaluate information, build accurate citations, archive source material, take notes, outline topics, and prepare to write.

Yes, NoodleTools will create citations according to MLA, APA, or Chicago Style standards, helping you properply format in-text citations and Works Cited (MLA), References (APA), or Bibliography (Chicago Style) to accompany your paper. While NoodleTools offers three citation levels, at West Essex we default to Advanced regardless of style guide.

While most students rely on NoodleTools primarily as citation management software, I want to reitrate that it's a research management platform. Try out some of its other features when you're feeling inspired: the digital notecards are very convient and work wonders for organizing both sources and your own thoughts; the outline tools can help you spot strengths and weaknesses in your argument before you draft a word; the collaborative projects both hasten groupwork and provide an easy avenue for teacher (or librarian!) feedback.

Name: NoveList
Description:
NoveList Plus is a readers' advisory database that helps you find your next read. Browse by genre or story element; search for similar titles and authors; set up alerts and receive a notification when your favorite writer publishes something new; see what's popular in current media; and rely on a bevy of lists and summaries to locate your new favorite book.  (Or you can, I dunno, talk to me. It's okay; I understand. The young people love the computer.)

One note: just because a book is on Novelist doesn't mean I have it in the library!

Name: Open Dissertations
Description:
EBSCO Open Dissertations is designed to increase traffic and discoverability of ETD research. You can join the movement and add your theses and dissertations to the database, making them freely available to researchers everywhere while increasing traffic to your institutional repository. This new resource extends the work started in 2014, when EBSCO and the H.W. Wilson Foundation created American Doctoral Dissertations which contained indexing from the H.W. Wilson print publication, Doctoral Dissertations Accepted by American Universities, 1933-1955. In 2015, the H.W. Wilson Foundation agreed to support the expansion of the scope of the American Doctoral Dissertations database to include records for dissertations and theses from 1955 to the present.

I see two main uses for this database at the high school level: if you're considering potential graduate study, it's a great way to preview standards and quality samples in a given field, and if you're researching a relatively niche topic, it's a boon to your bibliography to find a dissertation to mine.
Subjects: Social Studies|Culture and Geography|English Language Arts|Mathematics|Psychology|Science

Name: Gale Presents: Peterson's Test and Career Prep
Description:
Gale Presents: Peterson’s Test and Career Prep is an online learning resource that offers a central hub for standardized test prep, college planning, career assessment, job searches, and more. Test prep resources help users prepare for a variety of standardized exams, including college entry exams like the SAT and ACT, and vocational exams in industries like law enforcement, journeyman, cosmetology, as well as U.S. citizenship. Students can find college planning tools, including a school search and a scholarship search. Job seekers can take advantage of career exploration tools including career assessments, advice, help creating resumés and cover letters, and a job search engine. Plus, learners can find additional materials to brush up on foundational skills in math and science, reading and writing, and computer technology to support their future endeavors.

Remarkably underutilized.

Name: Points of View Ultimate
Description:
New for the 2026-2027 school year!

Points of View Ultimate provides diverse perspectives on hundreds of (over 750!) debate topics. It contains political magazines, newspapers, news transcripts, blog posts, primary sources, reference books and educational videos. Points of View Ultimate supports in-depth research into global issues, helping users analyze controversial topics, develop critical thinking and improve digital literacy.

The database covers hundreds of debate topics, each with Overview (objective background/description), Point (argument) and Counterpoint (opposing argument) articles and a Guide to Critical Analysis to help the reader evaluate the controversy, read more critically, develop their own perspective, and write or debate an effective argument.

A true step up from last year's POV database well worth giving a try!

Name: Pop Culture Universe
Description:
A one-of-a-kind social studies resource, Pop Culture Universe: Icons, Idols, Ideas examines U.S. history through developments in art, literature, clothing, fashion, food, film, music, sports, technology, and travel — all what students find interesting about today’s culture, in the context of America’s past. Thousands of primary and secondary sources organized in a decade-by-decade format support engaged learning about the movements, trends, and turning points that have shaped modern American history.

Don't treat this one like a search engine! Use the Decades pages to establish a basic overview of an era, then dive into the Stories and Analyze sections to take in the main trends, events, hot topics, and key questions informing the pop culture's development. Covers the 1900s through the 2010s.

Name: Primary Search
Description:
Primary Search is a full-text database of carefully curated content for elementary school libraries. It includes full text for the most popular children's magazines, e-books, and easy-to-read encyclopedic entries written specifically for kids.

Kids like little kids. Little little. Babysitting? Interested in child development or education? Dive in!

Name: Primary Search Reference eBook Collection
Description:
The Primary Search Reference eBook Collection is offered as a companion to Primary Search, containing reference books from top educational publishers and presses. This encompasses a broad range of general reference subject coverage for primary school students, with topics like social studies, history, language arts, geography, culture, math and science.

Kids like little kids. Little little. Babysitting? Interested in child development or education? Dive in!

Name: Professional Development Collection
Description:
Professional Development Collection is a highly specialized database of full-text electronic information especially for educators, professional librarians and education researchers.

Are you a teacher who's actually using this? Tell me! Please, please tell me.

Name: Referencia Latina
Description:
Referencia Latina es una base de datos en español a texto completo que cubre una amplia gama de temas dentro y fuera del ámbito académico. Ofrece contenidos de diversas fuentes, como libros de referencia, revistas de interés general e informes de salud. Las actualizaciones diarias garantizan la disponibilidad de los artículos más recientes de una docena de periódicos y noticiarios destacados de 12 países latinoamericanos.


Referencia Latina is a full-text Spanish database that covers a wide range of topics inside and outside of academia. It offers content from various sources, such as reference books, general interest magazines and health reports. Daily updates ensure the availability of the latest articles from a dozen leading newspapers and newscasts from 12 Latin American countries.

Name: Regional Business News
Description:
Regional Business News provides full-text regional business publications for the United States and Canadian provinces. Users can search newspapers, magazines and other resources from trusted news sources.  Content for Regional Business News is provided by leading publishers in business news. Key resources include newspapers, radio and television news transcripts, trade publications, magazines and newswires.

If you're researching a business-related topic and want to dive into localized economic data, this is the database for you. DECA and FBLA members: if you aren't consulting this resources as you prepare for your events, you're selling yourself short!

Name: Salem Press eBook Library
Description:
Salem Press offers reference volumes that focus on important events and developments in liteature, history, and science as well as essential critical thinking and study skills.

Although Salem's scope is narrow and its interface a bit dated, the content itself is high quality, especially the Critical Insights series.

Name: Science Online
Description:
Science Online offers expansive reference coverage of the full range of scientific disciplines through extensive essays, videos, diagrams, definitions, interactives, and experiments. Comprehensive Topic Centers help students find a starting point for their research, and the science eLearning modules cover core topics with Teacher Support. Topics include biology, chemistry, physics, earth and space sciences, environmental science, marine science, forensics, weather, computers, and math support.

This is a specialized database with an especially rich set of multimedia and fanastic pathfinders. It combines encylopedia-style aricles with videos, animations, diagrams, and interactive "experiments" accompanied by citations that actually explicate the sources behind each article. Make use of the topic centers and eLearning modules if you need some extra help wrapping your mind around a tricky concept.

Name: Science Reference eBook Collection
Description:
The Science Reference eBook Collection is offered as a companion to Science Reference Source, containing reference books from top educational publishers and university presses. This encompasses a rich selection of titles covering science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

Look here for book-length treatments that afford a level of insight and contextualization beyond the purview of an article.

Name: Science Reference Ultimate
Description:
Science Reference Ultimate is an online science research resource for high school students and teachers that provides full text for hundreds of science magazines, journals, reference books and high-quality videos. The database also contains science experiments, curriculum-aligned lesson plans, and a vast image collection. Topics include applied sciences, biology, chemistry, computer science, earth sciences, engineering, environmental science, forensics, health and wellness, mathematics, paleontology, physics, scientists and innovators, and space sciences and astronomy. Each category breaks down into popular, colloquial, or curriculum-based subtopics that are logical for all users and friendlier to younger or novice researchers. Clicking on the subtopic brings the user to a page with a topic overview, related subtopics and overview articles, sample search results (with the option to view all results) and a carousel of relevant e-books (if available).

EBSCO's science offerings are set apart by the sheer quantity of periodical articles available on a variety of topics. If you can't find it here, odds are you'll struggle elsewhere.

Name: Small Business Reference eBook Collection
Description:
The Small Business Reference eBook Collection is offered as a companion to Small Business Source, containing reference books from top educational publishers and presses. This encompasses a rich selection of titles centered on sustainable and ethical business practices for small businesses.

Ideal for the far-thinking planner who wants to go beyond bullet points and summaries.

Name: Small Business Source
Description:
Small Business Source offers exclusive full text for many top consumer small business reference books, as well as tools to understand and address a wide variety of small business topics. The database includes business videos, case studies, help and advice, a start-up kit and tips for writing business plans. Small Business Source offers a collection of state-specific resources with demographic data and other information to meet the needs of small business owners and entrepreneurs. Many of the full-text reference books are provided through Nolo, the nation’s oldest and most respected provider of legal information for consumers and small businesses. Business videos include interviews, lessons learned, lectures and how-to tips to foster success in all aspects of managing a business. Subjects include: starting and growing a business, writing a business plan, marketing a business, managing employees, going green, conducting business on the internet, understanding legal information, selling a business. 

A must for the aspiring entrepreneur. DECA and FBLA members: if you aren't consulting these resources as you prepare for your events, you're selling yourself short!

Name: Teacher Reference Center
Description:
Teacher Reference Center is a curated index of education magazines and peer-reviewed journals spanning the full breadth of professional topics in the field. Topics covered include assessment, best practices, continuing education, curriculum development, elementary education, higher education, instructional media, literacy standards, pedagogical research, school administration, teacher education, and more.

Are you a teacher? Do you actually use this? Please let me know!

Name: The Atlantic
Description:
The Atlantic is a long-running, influential American magazine known for its coverage and analysis of politics, foreign affairs, business, technology, culture, and more.

Here is the mission statement published in the very first issue of The Atlantic, in November 1857, and signed by many of the greats of American letters, including Ralph Waldo Emerson, Herman Melville, Harriet Beecher Stowe, and Nathaniel Hawthorne:

First: In Literature, to leave no province unrepresented, so that while each number will contain articles of an abstract and permanent value, it will also be found that the healthy appetite of the mind for entertainment in its various forms of Narrative, Wit, and Humor, will not go uncared for. The publishers wish to say, also, that while native writers will receive the most solid encouragement, and will be mainly relied on to fill the pages of The Atlantic, they will not hesitate to draw from the foreign sources at their command, as occasion may require, relying rather on the competency of an author to treat a particular subject, than on any other claim whatever. In this way they hope to make their Periodical welcome wherever the English tongue is spoken or read.

Second: In the term Art they intend to include the whole domain of aesthetics, and hope gradually to make this critical department a true and fearless representative of Art, in all its various branches, without any regard to prejudice, whether personal or national, or to private considerations of what kind soever.

Third: In Politics, The Atlantic will be the organ of no party or clique, but will honestly endeavor to be the exponent of what its conductors believe to be the American idea. It will deal frankly with persons and with parties, endeavoring always to keep in view that moral element which transcends all persons and parties, and which alone makes the basis of a true and lasting national prosperity. It will not rank itself with any sect of anties, but with that body of men which is in favor of Freedom, National Progress, and Honor, whether public or private.

Name: The New York Times
Description:
The New York Times is dedicated to helping people understand the world through on-the-ground, expert and deeply reported independent journalism.

Whatever one makes of its opinion writers, the Times is the first port of call for many news-seekers for a reason. Home to some of the finest journalists in the world and long considered the standardbearer of the American free press.

Name: TOPICsearch
Description:
Teachers, librarians and student researchers can use this database to explore current events, social, political and economic issues, scientific discoveries and other popular topics frequently discussed in the classroom. Source types include biographies, book reviews, government information, periodicals, public opinion polls, and international newspapers.

Another flavor of EBSCO; I'd suggest Explora unless you're specifically after information on recent events.

Name: World Book Online
Description:
World Book Online helps information seekers of all ages find the content they need at the correct reading level. The resources are available anytime, anywhere—at school and at home. A trusted encyclopedia of school and public libraries for decades, World Book Online contains thousands of informational articles with stunning illustrations, videos, interactive maps, research help, and activities.

Put this in a bucket with Brittanica and Explora: a great surface-level source and an amazing compendium on information, but not a destination for high school-level research in itself.

Name: World Geography and Culture
Description:
World Geography and Culture is the definitive resource for the study of countries, cultures, and geography concepts and skills. Every country of the world is profiled in depth, covering all aspects of its geography, history, society, and culture. At-a-glance information, maps and flags, videos, images, gazetteer entries, biographies of famous people, a timeline, and current news supplement each country profile. Comprehensive entries about the U.S. states are also available.

An expanded version of the sort of information you'd find in the dearly departed CIA World Factbook.

Name: World Religions
Description:
World Religions: Belief, Culture, and Controversy spans more than 50 religions practiced throughout the world, both those that have flourished and those that have disappeared. Important figures, core beliefs, customs and practices, celebrations and holidays, momentous events, significant and sacred places, and more accompany descriptions of the essence of each religion, and daily updates and additions aid researchers in their examination of the continuously metamorphosing role of religion. Topics include Buddhism, Christianity, Chinese Religions, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, New Religions, Shinto, Traditional Religions, Western Esotericism, Unbelief, and Other Faiths and Beliefs. This database was created under the advisory oversight of J. Gordon Melton, PhD, author of more than 40 scholarly texts and reference books on religion, and a Distinguished Senior Fellow of the Institute for Religious Studies at Baylor University in Texas.

An excellent resource for expanding your understanding not only of your own faith (or lack thereof), but to better understand the development and intersections of global religious traditions. However much you think you know about a given belief system, its history always proves more complicated than you initially suspected.
